questions.q: According to this lesson, what is explicitly out of scope for a job-ready cloud engineer's DR planning on a small environment?
options: Building active-active multi-region failover with a dedicated DR site, like an enterprise DR architect would
Knowing the system's RTO and RPO
Having a backup policy configured
Writing down a basic recovery procedure
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly scopes out enterprise-scale multi-region failover architecture as not what a cloud engineer owns for a small environment.

questions.q: What are the four pieces of a basic DR plan for a small environment, per this lesson?
options: Known RTO/RPO, a backup policy that satisfies them, restore-tested backups, and a documented recovery procedure
A dedicated DR site, a 24/7 NOC, automatic failover, and a compliance audit
Only a backup policy and nothing else
A list of every server in the environment with no other detail
questions.explain: The plan combines the outputs of the chapter's three earlier lessons (objectives, policy, tested proof) with a new documented recovery procedure.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a written recovery procedure still matters even if RTO/RPO, backup policy, and restore testing are all already done correctly?
options: Without written steps, someone has to improvise the actual recovery process for the first time during a real, pressured outage
A written procedure is only needed for compliance paperwork, not for the actual recovery
RTO and RPO automatically generate the recovery steps on their own
A written procedure replaces the need for backups entirely
questions.explain: Even with everything else correct, skipping the written procedure means someone improvises who does what and in what order during the actual incident.

questions.q: What does 'ownership' mean in the context of this lesson's DR plan?
options: A named person or role responsible for a system's recovery, decided before a disaster happens
Which cloud provider owns the resource being backed up
The billing account that pays for the backup storage
Whoever happens to be awake when the outage starts
questions.explain: Ownership means deciding, ahead of time, exactly who is responsible for recovering a given system — not sorting it out during the incident.

questions.q: How do this chapter's four lessons (17-20) relate to each other?
options: RTO/RPO set the objectives, the backup policy is configured to meet them, restore testing proves the backups work, and this lesson documents the procedure and owner into one DR plan
Each lesson covers a completely unrelated, independent topic
Lesson 20 replaces the need for Lessons 17 through 19
The lessons must be done in reverse order to work correctly
questions.explain: The chapter builds cumulatively: objectives drive the policy, the policy's backups get restore-tested, and the whole thing is written up as a DR plan with a named owner.
